content.jointProblem: Can an unsupervised, site-specific baseline model built from Modbus/BACnet traffic features, using adaptive change-point and control-chart methods with calibrated anomaly scores, detect behavioural drift without labelled attacks while producing plain-language alarms within the ProtoSense device latency budget? The first experiment would adapt Ostojić's multivariate SPC/change-point methods to packet-derived time series and test detection delay and false alarms on normal traffic plus simulated or red-team anomalies.

rationale.text: Ostojić's research directly addresses unsupervised anomaly detection under distribution shift and the absence of labelled fault data, which is the core constraint of ProtoSense.

sources.quote: Open challenges discussed include distribution shift under normal ageing, alarm rationalisation in dense sensor networks, and the absence of labelled fault data.
One-class support vector machines produce a real-valued decision score that can serve as a univariate control-chart statistic

rationale.text: She has developed online change-point and adaptive covariance/control-chart methods for non-stationary multivariate streams, a candidate basis for learning per-site traffic baselines.

sources.quote: a Bayesian online change-point detection model (BOCPD) extended to multivariate observations under a Normal-Inverse-Wishart conjugate prior
replacing the static covariance estimate with a sliding-window estimator updated at each sampling instant

rationale.text: Her work explicitly addresses calibration, threshold setting and interpretability of anomaly scores as control-chart statistics, relevant to alarms a plant manager can understand.

sources.quote: how to calibrate raw SVM scores to approximate a false-alarm probability
interpretability of run rules and average-run-length guarantees

rationale.text: She has worked on drift monitoring and recalibration of deployed anomaly detectors, which is needed to keep site-specific baselines valid over months.

sources.quote: two-level monitoring architecture in which a primary anomaly detector (isolation forest trained offline) is supervised by a secondary drift monitor

rationale.text: Her group has experience with multi-site and federated monitoring architectures that avoid centralising raw data, matching a vendor serving many client sites.

sources.quote: pool monitoring knowledge across sites without centralising raw sensor data for privacy or bandwidth reasons
federated monitoring architecture for multi-site deployment

rationale.text: She has prior paid consultancy replacing rule-based alarm systems with data-driven SPC and designing operator dashboards, supporting the explainability requirement.

sources.quote: carried out paid consultancy engagements for two manufacturers in the Vojvodina region
advising on the replacement of rule-based alarm systems with data-driven SPC methods and on the design of operator dashboards

rationale.text: Her stated participation is open to joint projects and contract research on anomaly detection and SPC system design.

sources.quote: contract research on anomaly detection and SPC system design

constraints.text: The method must be unsupervised and must not depend on supervised classifiers trained on public ICS attack datasets.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us

constraints.text: The plan must learn normal behaviour per site and use the company's consented traffic archives under NDA for training and evaluation.

sources.quote: What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline
access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA

constraints.text: Alarms must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language, not only as a raw anomaly score.

sources.quote: We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language

constraints.text: Inference must fit the planned on-device security processor without affecting packet forwarding latency.

sources.quote: dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: The researcher requires access to labelled or time-stamped operational data from real systems.

sources.quote: particularly interested in collaborators who can provide access to labelled or time-stamped operational data from real production systems

constraints.text: The collaboration must respect Ostojić's stated limit on extensive hardware integration and embedded firmware work.

sources.quote: not in a position to take on projects requiring extensive hardware integration or embedded firmware development beyond lightweight deployment of pre-trained models

risks: Ostojić's evidence is in process and sensor SPC, not Modbus/BACnet network traffic or intrusion detection; the transfer to packet-derived features is unproven and must be the first experiment.
No labelled attacks exist, so detection performance can only be assessed through proxies such as red-team or simulated anomalies and careful false-alarm analysis.
ProtoSense integration in C/Rust may exceed the researcher's stated embedded scope; company engineers would need to own firmware integration.
Ostojić's availability is unknown and not confirmed by any source.
Client traffic is under NDA and heterogeneous across sites; data access and per-site normal definitions may limit how much can be shared or generalised.
The company's prior academic collaboration was a one-semester student project that was not continued formally, so joint-project management is relatively untested.
questions: What effort and start date can Ostojić commit, and should the work be structured as a joint project or as an industrial PhD with a company engineer as candidate?
Which time-stamped Modbus/BACnet captures and site metadata can be shared under NDA, and do they include change logs or operator context needed to define normal behaviour?
How should packet traffic be converted into multivariate time-series features: flows, function codes, BACnet objects, timing, or parser outputs already available in ProtoSense?
What detection and false-alarm targets will be used without labelled attacks, and can ArmaturaSec generate red-team or simulated malicious traffic for testing?
What is the target hardware and latency budget, and who owns integration of a trained model versus firmware development in C/Rust?
What form of plain-language explanation does a plant manager need, and what alarm-rationalisation process exists?
Can ArmaturaSec provide the stated one to two part-time engineers and hardware bench access, and is there a specific engineer who would work with the researcher?
Are there legal or data-protection constraints on using client traffic from multiple countries for model training and benchmarking?
